title: Remarketing Terms Table: Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Reinstatement, Sale and Deficiency Figures
content:
**Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract — post-repossession figures.**

| Tier | Company reinstatement window (calendar days after repossession) | Company reinstatements over the life of the contract |
|---|---|---|
| Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Tier 5 | 10 | 1 |
| Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Tier 4 | 10 | 1 |
| Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Tier 3 | 15 | 1 |
| Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Tier 2 | 15 | 1 |
| Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Tier 1 | 21 | 2 |
| Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Tier 1+ | 21 | 2 |

Figures common to every tier:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Days past due on another Kestrel account at which a discretionary reinstatement is withheld | 30 |
| Company minimum calendar days between the notice of intent to sell and the sale | 15 |
| Surplus refunded within | 30 calendar days after the sale |
| Minimum lump-sum deficiency settlement | 60 percent of the deficiency balance |
| Unpaid deficiency charged off no earlier than | 90 calendar days after the sale |

## Reading the table

- The reinstatement count is a ceiling the reinstatements already used must stay below: a Tier 1 contract that has used 1 reinstatement is below its figure of 2.
- The 30-day relationship figure includes its own value: another Kestrel account at exactly 30 days past due withholds a discretionary reinstatement; one at 29 does not.
- A settlement offer of exactly 60 percent of the deficiency balance meets the minimum; a hypothetical deficiency of 5,000.00 dollars needs a lump sum of at least 3,000.00 dollars.
